quest.title: The End of the Sabzeruz Festival
quest.description: Discovering the truth behind the samsara of the Sabzeruz Festival is not enough. You still need to find a way to break out of it. The good news is, you now see a glimmer of hope...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x725, Primogem x30, Mora x29025, Memory of Flourishing Green x1, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x5

chapter.title: The Morn a Thousand Roses Brings

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Good morning, Nahida! Wait... Now that Paimon remembers everything, should we instead say, "Good morning, Lesser Lord Kusanali"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, what's wrong, Nahida? You don't look too good...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...I'm afraid that what you're thinking right now is correct...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Did Dunyarzad already disappear? No way! Are... Are we too late?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The real Dunyarzad's consciousness has indeed disappeared. It can no longer endure the constant dream harvesting.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon can't believe it... Wait, so what about that other Dunyarzad? Just what is she? Is she also going to disappear?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: She's actually something like a puppet, but not completely.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: The real Dunyarzad's consciousness could no longer keep playing her role in this dream...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: So, another Dunyarzad appeared to replace her in the dream. Just like the grass and the trees, that Dunyarzad is just a building block of the dream that helps to keep it going.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But personality-wise, she's nothing like the real Dunyarzad...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Puppets are stiff and can't copy a living person's vitality. After all, they're just there as filler.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: You know, speaking of which... The old Dunyarzad might not have been too different from a puppet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Dunyarzad truly believed that she met you within her consciousness, and it was you who inspired her... So you do remember her after all!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes. Back then, her family was overly protective of her. No one cared about her personality or thoughts. It was as if she only lived to stall her Eleazar.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I just gave her a little wisdom so she could look at life in a new way... So that she could be her own person. But even so, she still...

choices.text: It still meant a lot to her.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Far from it. I'm still a long way off from being a real archon.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I couldn't even save her. If I were a competent archon, I wouldn't have let my most faithful follower die at the Sabzeruz Festival with so many regrets...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Please don't beat yourself up over it, Nahida! It's the Sages' fault, and theirs alone!

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: I... I'm not beating myself up. All I did was to rationally observe the distance between myself and a real archon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't be like that, Nahida. Even real archons are still allowed to be sad...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: To prevent more tragedies like this, we must end the samsara as soon as possible.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Great! But how do we do that?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Although this Sabzeruz Festival dream is under the Akasha's control, only humans can dream. Even the Akasha is unable to create them.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: That means this dream belongs to a host who created it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... So how should we find that person?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Well, if this is someone's dream, then everything here must come from deep within their consciousness ...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...Which means, with the power of imagination, they can change anything in this dream.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Imagination? What do you mean by that?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Imagination means breaking through what you perceive as normal.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Like when a server at a tavern brings a plate to you, you'd naturally assume that food is on it.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: However, if you're the dream's host and you become aware that you're dreaming, when you imagine gold and Mora on the plate...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: ...The dream will respond in kind, and the server really will bring you gold and Mora.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: But right now, our host is unaware that this is a dream. No matter how many times they're served, it will always be food.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So we find the host — then what?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Find some way to make that person realize that they're dreaming. Usually, once that happens, the person will wake up and the dream's samsara will be broken.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How are we going to find them, though? If it could be anyone, it'd be like looking for a needle in a haystack!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And even if we did find them, how are we supposed to make them realize they're dreaming?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: After all, like you said... "Don't wake a sleepwalker."

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: It's extremely difficult, yes. But the only ones who can do it are you two. Remember, everything you've achieved up to this point has all been for the sake of finding the host and ending the samsara.

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: As for me... during this time, I'll be out of town.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: "Out of town"? Are you going to that place full of dreams where the Traveler went?

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Yes, I want to try something. There must still be a small wisp of possibility...

response.speaker: Nahida
response.text: Hurry and go. Dreams are supposed to be fantastical, romantic, and full of pleasant surprises. Unnecessary things like this samsara... need to end.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* Paimon's still a little upset that we've come this far, only for Dunyarzad to...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She was such a good person with such a simple wish, but fate was against her.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I just feel so demoralized.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah... Saving Dunyarzad is what kept us going this whole time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But we mustn't lose hope, Traveler! Dunyarzad would definitely want to see us save everyone else. So let's break this samsara for her sake!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's wondering... Do you think the sages would get one of their own to be the host of this dream? Feels like it would be easier to control it that way, no?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Unlikely.

choices.text: Knowing the plan, they'd probably become aware that they were dreaming.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh, that's true. Plus, the sages probably weren't counting on there being other factors beyond their control — like Nahida and us.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, who do you think the host of the dream is?

choices.text: Maybe Farris, the Knight of Flowers?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh! That would make sense! Farris, the Knight of Flowers, is a symbol of the whole Sabzeruz Festival, right? Pretty core character.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Let's go ask him some questions, shall we?

choices.text: The one with the strange get-up?
An unsuspecting host would be less likely to realize this is a dream.

talks.objective: Talk to Farris, the Knight of Flowers

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Hm? You're back. You left in a hurry last time. Is everything okay?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Everything's fine, just... Umm, it's a little hard to explain. Uh, would you mind taking part in a little experiment with us?

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: An experiment? That came out of nowhere... I'm listening, though. What do you need me to do?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Could you... make a wish?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Imagine your wish coming true before your very eyes.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: You want me to make a wish? Is that a new Sabzeruz Festival tradition or something?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Less questions, more wishing!

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Okay, okay...

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: My wish, my wish... Um, okay, I'm a little nervous saying this out loud, but... I want Miss Dunyarzad to be happy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh...

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: I noticed earlier that she looked a bit down, and she wasn't really talking to anyone.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: She just doesn't seem like herself. She's always so gentle and kind, and all the kids love her...

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: I've also wondered if the reason she asked me to be Farris, Knight of Flowers is because I'm special to her, or something...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... you have a crush on Dunyarzad?

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Uh, heh... Haha... Is it that obvious? Hmm, after what I just said, I guess it is.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: When she placed the hat of the Knight of Flowers onto my head, she said to me, "I want everyone to have a happy Sabzeruz Festival."

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: What she didn't realize was that I'm not that interested in how everyone else feels... In that moment, I just wanted to be her Knight of Flowers for the rest of my life. Fifty years, a hundred years... I'll serve her till the end of time.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: ...Okay, yeah, that was a bit much. Felt like the right moment to get it off my chest, but... ahem, that was pretty embarrassing.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Okay, I'm ready to make my wish: I would like Miss Dunyarzad to appear in front of me right now, with a smile on her face... Here goes...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Please come true...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Please come true...

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: I'm gonna open my eyes, ho-ho!

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Oh... You're...!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What!?

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: ...Phaki? Sorry, but only one portion of Yalda Candies per person. Back home you go.

dialogues.speaker: Vihar
dialogues.text: Hahaha... Nice try, you two. Anyway, never mind, I don't need to see her appear right in front of me. As long as she's happy, hahaha...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *sigh* Guess he isn't the host of this dream after all. Should've expected it wouldn't be this easy.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It seems like everyone who knows Dunyarzad loves her, but none of them has any idea that she...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: My lady, step back!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds like Dehya! Oh, right, this is when Dunyarzad bumps into the kidnappers.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'll teach them a lesson they won't forget.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? But Dehya can handle them... Hey, Traveler!

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...Oh? It's you. Great timing! Please take—

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: Hey, this is my job. The Homayanis pay me, not you.

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: You... Ugh, alright fine, knock yourself out. Why are you so worked up anyway? It's not like I don't trust your fighting skills...

response.speaker: Dehya
response.text: ...Anyway, watch yourself.

response.speaker: Badis
response.text: So you got yourself some back-up? Hmph, suit yourself! You're goin' down!

talks.objective: Defeat all the ambushing Eremite members

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Traveler... Were you just taking your anger out on those guys?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *sigh* You and Nahida both... Dunyarzad wouldn't want to see you two like this.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, and speaking of her... Paimon just remembered something.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Remember how during the first Sabzeruz Festival, before the samsara started, we came here with Dunyarzad because she wanted to pick something up?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She said it was because she had forgotten something.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Okay, so Paimon's memory is working so far... Anyway, Paimon also remembers that she's staying somewhere around here. She pointed it out to us the night before the Sabzeruz Festival.

choices.text: Should we check out what the item is?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, even if it's only a tiny clue, it'll probably still help us more than this needle-in-a-haystack search...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This is the place. It's rude to enter other people's spaces without permission, but desperate times call for desperate measures!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, the windows are unlocked. Okay, Paimon's gonna take a peek inside.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Paimon enters the room and returns a while later, carrying something...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: This was only a temporary residence, so there was pretty much nothing inside except this book on the table.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Should we open it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow... Dunyarzad wrote all of this. Sounds like she was always thinking of us, even while we were away...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Even though she was also busy preparing for the Sabzeruz Festival, and had all her health problems to worry about...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She must have wanted to give this to us as a gift on the day of the Sabzeruz Festival, right?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: If we hadn't found this book, we never would have known...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But now that we know, we can't even thank her...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Dunyarzad...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, where are you off to now?

choices.text: Maybe it'll give us some clues.
Ah yes. I'd forgotten all about that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's Dunyarzad's puppet...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Thank you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Traveler...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You must be exhausted.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come to think of it, we've been stuck in this place for a really, really long time. Heck, even the last time we were chatting happily with Dunyarzad feels like an eternity ago...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon still remembers when we were sitting here, and the way her eyes sparkled when she talked about Nilou's Dance of Sabzeruz...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: ...I can barely recall it now.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: ...There will always be frustrations in life, but I know that the point of living is to not leave behind any regrets.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That was what the real Dunyarzad said, wasn't it? Does that mean...!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Dunyarzad...?

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Yes, Traveler? What is it?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh... So she's still just a puppet. But just now... How come...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? Where are we going this time?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: To watch the Dance of Sabzeruz.

choices.text: (I'll feel better if I say this out loud...)

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: If you continue to resist, we will have to order an investigation into every single event organizer...

dialogues.speaker: Setaria
dialogues.text: The Grand Sage has already granted you much leniency. I advise that you exercise tact.

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: How... How did things turn out like this...

dialogues.speaker: Nilou
dialogues.text: Ahh... Traveler? You don't have to get involved. He's a sage from the Akademiya. I don't want to drag you into this...

dialogues.speaker: Azar
dialogues.text: ...Traveler?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Traveler, what the heck are you doing!? If you get arrested by the Akademiya, that's another day gone to waste!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... They're not reacting! Have they been scared stiff...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, of course! If this is the sages' plan, they wouldn't put themselves through this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So they're just substitutes.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: What is this? What happened to the Grand Sage and his entourage?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Hehe, like I said, they symbolize the Goddess of Flowers, after all. It's just a shame that all the real Padisarahs went extinct after her death.

response.speaker: Dunyarzad
response.text: Yes. The Greater Lord brought forth new Padisarahs in memory of the Goddess of Flowers, but she ultimately could never truly replicate that beautiful shade of purple.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Ahh, "that beautiful shade of purple"... Aren't these flowers real Padisarahs, just like the ones from the legend? I didn't even notice! Dunyarzad, did you find these?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But didn't you just say all the real flowers went extinct after the Goddess of Flowers passed away? So how...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Yeah. What's going on here...?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Nilou, close your eyes.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Imagine that the Grand Sage and his entourage are not here in front of you.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: You guys are acting weird... But okay, I'll try.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Mmm...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Hey~

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Th—They disappeared! So Nilou's the host. What a surprise!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Purple Padisarahs don't exist in the real world anymore, but in Nilou's subconscious, they can appear as decorations on the stage.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It's just like the example Nahida told us. People assume there will be food on a plate, and Nilou assumed there would be real Padisarahs in the flower pots.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So when you saw the flowers, you instantly knew it was Nilou?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Correct.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: But if we want to end the samsara, we need the host to become aware that they're dreaming.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How should we make Nilou realize that...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Am I dreaming?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh!?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: How did you come to that conclusion?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Hehe, so I'm right? Is this Lesser Lord Kusanali responding to our celebration of the Sabzeruz Festival?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wrong guess, but you aren't completely wrong, either... The point is, what made you think this is a dream?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: As far as you know, people in Sumeru don't dream, right?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Yeah, but have you heard the tale of the First Sage? To prevent a calamity, he went on a journey to find the Dendro Archon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, sounds familiar! Dunyarzad told us a story like that when we first arrived in Sumeru City. So it was about the First Sage, huh?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Yep, but in the part you heard, he hadn't become the First Sage yet. There's more to the story...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: His piety and wisdom were acknowledged by the Dendro Archon, and she finally gave her blessing to him.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: All kinds of spectacular scenes appeared in front of the First Sage, as if all the knowledge in the world was being painted onto a canvas right before him. He was captivated.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: After who knows how long, he mastered all the knowledge he could comprehend.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Afterward, he said to the Dendro Archon, "I miss my parents, my wife, and my children. I've been away from home for far too long. They must be worried."

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: The Dendro Archon smiled. The next second, the sage found himself lying in his bed, as if he had just woken up from a dream.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: His wife, lying next to him, said: "You're off to search for the Dendro Archon today, aren't you? Have a safe journey, my love."

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: In the end, the First Sage took care of many disasters in Sumeru City and founded the Akademiya. What a happy ending!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So... The First Sage was dreaming ever since the beginning of the story? He never went on his journey?

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Yes, but his faith and determination were conveyed to the Dendro Archon, so she blessed him in the form of a dream.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon understands where you're coming from now. That's a really interesting connection... But we really gotta wake up soon, like the sage in the story.

choices.text: Now that Nilou is aware of it...

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: I see. Well, it just so happens that today's Sabzeruz Festival is almost over, too.

response.speaker: Nilou
response.text: Since we're in a dream, let's make this final Dance of Sabzeruz as beautiful as we can!

choices.text: I've been waiting a long time for this.
This dream should be over soon.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: *yawn* Good morning, Traveler. Paimon feels like she's been asleep for the longest time...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Paimon's head feels super heavy. Did we oversleep? ...Do you even remember going to sleep last night?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon thinks it was... after the Sabzeruz Festival...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: *gasp* The Sabzeruz Festival!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Have we finally escaped from the Sabzeruz samsara?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: I remember now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Quick, take off your Akasha Terminal!

choices.text: At the end of the Dance of Sabzeruz, I think I saw...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She's not in her room. What happened?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Let's go to the usual spot!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? What usual spot?

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne?
dialogues.text: Well done, Traveler and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne?
dialogues.text: And... Thank you, Dunyarzad, for organizing the Sabzeruz Festival for me.

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I'm sorry, who are—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Dunyarzad! *sniff* *sniff* You're okay! Oh, don't scare us like that...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Dunyarzad...

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: Oh! Traveler, Paimon! I have something amazing to tell you!

dialogues.speaker: Dunyarzad
dialogues.text: I just had a dream... and I saw Nilou performing the Dance of Sabzeruz!

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Ugh, okay.

dialogues.speaker: Merchant
dialogues.text: *sigh* How am I supposed to conduct business when I'm not allowed to leave the city?

dialogues.speaker: Guard
dialogues.text: Hey! Stop right there! No one is allowed to enter or leave Sumeru City right now. Go away!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa... Ugh, okay.
